title: SLOs + Oncall Escalation & Capacity Trigger Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This playbook defines how SRE measures and enforces service-level objectives (SLOs), links SLO consumption to oncall escalation, and defines capacity triggers that must surface to product and infra teams. It contains concrete burn-rate thresholds, alert-to-action mappings, capacity-forecast triggers, and reproducible escalation templates (PagerDuty, Slack, email). Use this as the canonical reference for SRE-led operational responses related to SLO and capacity risk.

Scope

- Applies to all customer-facing Redwood services in the Hosted and Dedicated fleets (examples: ingest-api, model-router, generation-service, embeddings-service).
- Not intended for internal tooling without customer impact (see internal tooling runbooks).

Definitions

- SLO: The measurable target for a service (e.g., availability, latency).
- Error budget: 1 - SLO (time or request-weighted over a rolling window).
- Burn rate: Ratio of error budget used per unit time relative to the nominal rate.
- Alert: A signal from monitoring indicating metric degradation.
- Page: Phone/SMS/Push using PagerDuty (critical paging).

Baseline SLOs (examples)

- ingest-api: Availability SLO 99.9% (monthly rolling window). Monthly error budget ≈ 0.1% of minutes (~43.2 minutes for a 30-day month).
- model-router: P95 response latency SLO < 300ms (30-day window, request-weighted).
- generation-service: Availability SLO 99.5% (monthly) for non-billing customers, 99.9% for enterprise SLA customers.

Measurement & Instrumentation Requirements

- SLO signal sources: production Prometheus/Grafana metrics for request_success_count and request_total; synthetic transactions for end-to-end availability; tracing-derived latency histograms.
- SLO calculation frequency: 1 minute rollup, stored as 1-minute SLO windows and aggregated to 1h/24h/30d views.
- Recording rule examples (PromQL):
  - availability_ratio = sum(rate(request_success_count[5m])) / sum(rate(request_total[5m]))
  - p95_latency_ms = histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) * 1000
- Dashboarding: Every SLO must have a dedicated Grafana panel (30d, 7d, 1d) and an SLO summary panel with error budget remaining.

Error Budget Burn Policy (Actions mapped to burn rate)

- Low burn (burn rate < 2): Monitor, auto-triage if there is a correlated alert. No paging.
- Elevated (2 <= burn rate < 5 for > 30m): SRE oncall receives an informational notification (PagerDuty non-critical, Slack #incidents-monitoring). Owner review required within 30 minutes.
- Critical (burn rate >= 5 for > 15m): Trigger a critical page to SRE primary and service owner. Immediate mitigation required (see runbook).
- Sustained depletion (error budget consumed >= 50% in < 24h): Schedule a short-term remediation meeting (within 4 hours) with product and infra stakeholders; consider temporary traffic shaping or feature throttles.
- Exhausted (0% remaining): Enterprise SLA customers: automatic failover to backup model variant or Dedicated capacity slot if configured; notify customer-facing teams and initiate postmortem. For non-SLA: reduce non-critical features, enable lower-cost fallbacks per routing policy.

Burn rate detection rules (examples)

- Burn rate calculation: (error_budget_used in last 1h) / (error_budget_allowed_per_hour).
- Prometheus alert snippets (illustrative):
  - name: ErrorBudgetCritical
    expr: (sum(increase(request_failed_total[1h])) / sum(increase(request_total[1h]))) / (1 - SLO_target) > 5
    for: 15m
  - name: ErrorBudgetElevated
    expr: (sum(increase(request_failed_total[30m])) / sum(increase(request_total[30m]))) / (1 - SLO_target) > 2
    for: 30m

Oncall Integration and Escalation Flow

1) Detection
  - Metric alert or synthetic ping fails; alert routes to the service-specific Grafana/Atlas alerting rule.
2) Triage (automated)
  - Alert enrichment adds recent deploys, active incidents, and top error traces (via tracing link).
  - The alert runbook is attached to the PagerDuty incident.
3) Preliminary human triage (SRE first responder)
  - Verify signal validity (check for noisy exporters, pagination/rollups).
  - If false positive, close and annotate the alert.
  - If valid, execute the service-specific SLO runbook steps (see Runbook section).
4) Escalation
  - If critical burn threshold reached, page SRE primary + service owner.
  - After 10 minutes with no acknowledgement, escalate to SRE secondary and engineering manager.
  - After 30 minutes, page on-call for product and infra leads.

PagerDuty page template (critical)

- Title: [CRITICAL] {service} SLO burn-rate {burn_rate}x — {short symptom}
- Body:
  Service: {service}
  SLO: {slo_name} ({slo_target})
  Current burn rate: {burn_rate} (over {window})
  Error budget remaining: {percent}%
  Top alert: {alert_name}
  Immediate ask: Join {#incidents-{service}} or dial {conference_link} and follow runbook: {runbook_link}
  Links: Grafana panel | Traces | Recent deploys | Capacity dashboard

Slack escalation template (when alert is non-critical)

- Channel: #incidents-{service} (or #incidents-monitoring for cross-service)
- Message: :warning: {service} elevated SLO burn ({burn_rate}x). Please review dashboard: {grafana_link}. If you are oncall owner, ping @sre-oncall.

Runbook: High SLO Burn (quick checklist)

1) Identify failure mode:
  - Check recent deploys: git rev, image tag, helm release (CI/CD UI link).
  - Query top error codes and request paths (PromQL / traces).
  - Check external dependencies (upstream models, third-party APIs).
2) Triage mitigation (pick first available):
  - Rollback recent deploy to last-known-good (if deploy correlates with onset).
  - Increase capacity (scale replica count or spin a dedicated capacity slot for enterprise tenants).
  - Apply traffic shaping: reduce non-critical feature rollout percentages, apply rate-limits to noisy clients.
  - Enable cached responses / prefix-KV cache warmup for repetitive tokens.
3) Post-mitigation verification:
  - Observe error rate drop for 15 minutes and confirm burn rate has fallen below 2x before de-escalating.
4) Document actions in the PagerDuty incident and mark for postmortem if error budget > 50% consumed or customer impact occurred.

Capacity Triggers and Forecasting

- Daily capacity health check: SRE runs an automated job that reports per-service utilization (GPU vCPU, active model sessions, memory, queue length) and projects 7/30-day consumption based on trailing 7-day load.
- Thresholds that must create immediate tickets:
  - Expected 7-day demand growth > 80% of available spare capacity for a model family.
  - Queue length > 2x median and P95 latency for that queue crosses SLO by > 30%.
  - Sustained CPU/GPU utilization > 85% for > 6 hours for Dedicated pools.
- Decision actions when thresholds hit:
  - <2 weeks runway: open an urgent capacity request to Infra (cc product, sales if enterprise customers impacted).
  - <72 hours runway: execute rapid provisioning play (activate burst capacity, spin reserved nodes in cloud, or move lower-priority workloads to deferred buckets).

Capacity request template (ticket fields)

- Service: {service}
- Model family: {model}
- Reason: {sudden spike | sustained growth | scheduled event}
- Current utilization: {gpu%, vcpu%}
- Runway: {hours/days}
- Proposed mitigation: {burst, reserve, throttle}
- Owners: {service_owner, infra_owner}

Operational Tooling & Integrations

- PagerDuty: primary paging channel; SRE policy configured for burn-rate alerts and capacity runouts.
- Grafana: SLO dashboards with alert links and runbook attachments.
- BigQuery / DataLake: long-term SLO history and incident annotation store (used for retros).
- Slack: #incidents-{service}, #sre-ops, #capacity-planning; automated postings include links to dashboards and playbooks.
- Runbook storage: Confluence canonical page link included in all alerts; service runbooks must be kept under /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/{service_name}-runbook.

Incident Review & Postmortem Standards (minimum requirements)

- When required: Any incident where error budget > 50% consumed, outage > 15 minutes for customers, or enterprise SLA customers affected.
- Template must include: timeline (UTC), detection method, root cause analysis, action items (owner + due date), mea culpa communications, and a clear signal-to-prevent recurrence (test/monitoring/deployment change).
- Severity classification: Sev1 (customer-facing outage), Sev2 (partial impact / high degradation), Sev3 (minor). Each Sev1/Sev2 must have a postmortem published within 7 business days.

Example incident review checklist:

1) Assemble timeline from automated logs/traces (UTC).
2) Run RCA: code/regression, capacity, dependency, config, data, external.
3) Identify permanent fixes and add tests/alerts to prevent regression.
4) Assign owners and target dates (no more than 4 weeks for high priority fixes).

Ownership and RACI (summary)

- SRE: metrics, burn-rate alerts, first-line mitigation, capacity forecasts.
- Service Owner (product/engineering): fix root cause, roll forward or rollback decisions, remediation code changes.
- Infra: provisioning, cluster-level scaling, reserve capacity operations.
- Customer Success / Sales: customer comms for SLA-impacting incidents.

Appendix A — Useful PromQL snippets

- Error rate over 1h: sum(increase(request_failed_total[1h])) / sum(increase(request_total[1h]))
- Error budget remaining (approx): 1 - avg_over_time(error_rate[30d]) / (1 - slo_target)
